# runtimev1

```go
import runtimev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/runtime/v1"
```

Package runtimev1 is the runtime/v1 contract: what runs a multisite host's instances (ext/pocker as isolates, ext/docker in containers). A host runs exactly one: every instance runs on it. When more than one is registered, \`providers: { runtime/v1: docker }\` picks.

A host-scope service contract: providers register on the host's scope (ProvideIn), not on an app.

Source: [`ext/contracts/runtime/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/runtime/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Runtime]("runtime/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is runtime/v1, on a host's scope.

## Types

### Exit

```go
type Exit struct {
	InstanceID string
	Err        error
	// Restarting: the runtime starts the instance again right away (its pb_hooks or settings changed), so the host
	// reports it as starting and asks its health endpoint again instead of reporting it idle.
	Restarting bool
}
```

Exit is an instance's process ending. Err is nil for a stop the runtime chose (idle, powered off, removed, restarting with new settings or files) and set when it ended on its own (crashed, exited during startup).

### ExitNotifier

```go
type ExitNotifier interface {
	OnExit(fn func(Exit))
}
```

ExitNotifier tells the host each time an instance stops running (or fails to start), so the host's supervisor knows without polling. The host calls OnExit once, before Start. The runtime calls fn synchronously, in order, possibly while it holds its own locks, so fn must return quickly and never call back into the runtime from that goroutine.

### HealthChecker

```go
type HealthChecker interface {
	HealthCheck(instanceID string) (path string, anyStatus bool)
}
```

HealthChecker tells the host's supervisor how to ask a started instance whether it's up: the path (default /api/health) and whether any answer from the instance counts, not only 200 (releases without a health endpoint). Without it the host asks /api/health and wants 200.

### Prechecker

```go
type Prechecker interface {
	Precheck(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, inst sourcev1.Instance) bool
}
```

Prechecker runs before the gates admit a request for a local instance, e.g. to answer 503 for an instance under maintenance, without counting it against rate limits. false = answered.

### RunningLister

```go
type RunningLister interface {
	RunningIDs() []string
}
```

RunningLister lists the instances running now, including ones adopted at Start (containers that kept running across a host restart), so the host's supervisor can confirm them.

### Runtime

```go
type Runtime interface {
	// Name identifies the runtime ("pocker", "docker"), for logs and the host's startup lines.
	Name() string
	// Serves reports whether this runtime can run inst (e.g. its PocketBase version); the host refuses one it can't.
	Serves(inst sourcev1.Instance) bool
	// ServeInstance serves a request for inst, starting it on demand. The host has already resolved the instance,
	// admitted the request (gates) and decided it runs here.
	ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, inst sourcev1.Instance)
	// Ready reports whether the runtime can take requests.
	Ready() bool
}
```

Runtime runs instances on this host.

### Shutdowner

```go
type Shutdowner interface {
	Shutdown()
}
```

Shutdowner is called when the host stops.

### Starter

```go
type Starter interface {
	Start(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

Starter runs once before the host listens, e.g. to adopt containers that kept running across a restart. An error stops the host from starting.

### Statser

```go
type Statser interface {
	RunningCount() int
}
```

Statser reports how many instances it has running, for the health route.

### Syncer

```go
type Syncer interface {
	Sync(c sourcev1.Change, prev *sourcev1.Instance)
}
```

Syncer hears directory changes (stop removed instances, restart changed ones).
